name: Poisson random measures exist
statement:
ProbabilityTheory.exists_isPoissonRandomMeasure.{u} {E : Type u} [MeasurableSpace E]
  (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [MeasureTheory.SFinite ν] :
  ∃ Ω x P N, MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧ ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure N ν P
scope_note: Every s-finite intensity, on a probability space in the same universe.

name: Laplace functional of a Poisson random measure
scope_note: All measurable f >= 0, sigma-finite intensity, exp(-infinity) = 0.

name: Poisson random measures with the same intensity have the same law
statement:
ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure.map_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {Ω' : Type u_2}
  {E : Type u_3} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ' : MeasurableSpace Ω'} [MeasurableSpace E]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {P' : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} {N : Ω → MeasureTheory.Measure E}
  {N' : Ω' → MeasureTheory.Measure E} {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite ν]
  (hN : ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure N ν P)
  (hN' : ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure N' ν P') :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map N P = MeasureTheory.Measure.map N' P'
scope_note: Sigma-finite intensity. Uniqueness from simple functions, not from compactly supported functions alone.

name: Binomial point processes converge to a Poisson random measure
statement:
ProbabilityTheory.tendstoInLawVaguely_sumDiracRange.{u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace E]
  [TopologicalSpace E] [T2Space E] [LocallyCompactSpace E] [RegularSpace E] [OpensMeasurableSpace E]
  {μ : ℕ → MeasureTheory.Measure E} [∀ (n : ℕ), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (μ n)]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [ν.Regular]
  (h : MeasureTheory.Measure.TendstoVaguely (fun n => ↑n • μ n) Filter.atTop ν) {Ω' : Type u_3}
  {mΩ' : MeasurableSpace Ω'} {N' : Ω' → MeasureTheory.Measure E} {P' : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'}
  (hN' : ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure N' ν P') :
  ProbabilityTheory.TendstoInLawVaguely (fun n z => ProbabilityTheory.sumDiracRange n z)
    (fun n => MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi fun x => μ n) Filter.atTop N' P' ν
scope_note: Convergence in law is defined through joint counts on disjoint relatively compact continuity sets, not as weak convergence on a space of point measures: the library puts no topology on that space.

name: Point process of exceedances, time-space
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measureReal_sumDiracRange_timeSpace_eq.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {F G : CumulativeDistributionFunction} {As : ℕ → AffineIncrEquiv} {u : ℝ}
  (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  (hF : ∀ (i : ℕ) (x : ℝ), P.real {ω | X i ω ≤ x} = ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x)
  (hlim :
    ∀ (x : ℝ),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(As n • F).toStieltjesFunction x ^ n) Filter.atTop
        (nhds (↑G.toStieltjesFunction x)))
  (hu : 0 < ↑G.toStieltjesFunction u) {Ω' : Type u_2} {mΩ' : MeasurableSpace Ω'}
  {N' : Ω' → MeasureTheory.Measure (ℝ × ℝ)} {P' : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'}
  (hN' :
    ProbabilityTheory.IsPoissonRandomMeasure N'
      ((MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 1)).prod
        (ExtremeValueTheory.exceedanceMeasure G hu))
      P')
  {k : ℕ} {s t : Fin k → ℝ} {C : Fin k → Set ℝ} (hs : ∀ (j : Fin k), 0 ≤ s j)
  (hst : ∀ (j : Fin k), s j ≤ t j) (ht : ∀ (j : Fin k), t j ≤ 1)
  (hC : ∀ (j : Fin k), ExtremeValueTheory.IsExceedanceInterval G u (C j))
  (hd : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint fun j => Set.Ioc (s j) (t j) ×ˢ C j)) (m : Fin k → ℕ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      P.real
        {ω |
          ∀ (j : Fin k),
            (ProbabilityTheory.sumDiracRange n fun i => ((↑i + 1) / ↑n, (As n) (X i ω)))
                (Set.Ioc (s j) (t j) ×ˢ C j) =
              ↑(m j)})
    Filter.atTop (nhds (P'.real {ω | ∀ (j : Fin k), (N' ω) (Set.Ioc (s j) (t j) ×ˢ C j) = ↑(m j)}))
scope_note: Joint counts on disjoint time rectangles over exceedance intervals above u with G(u) > 0, not convergence on the compactified space.

name: De Haan's spectral representation of max-stable processes, constructive direction
scope_note: Constructive direction only, and finite-dimensional laws only: that every max-stable process has such a representation is not proved.

name: The Skorokhod space D[0,1] is separable
statement:
SkorokhodSpace.instSeparableSpace.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [PseudoEMetricSpace E]
  [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace E] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (SkorokhodSpace E)
scope_note: Time set [0,1], values in a separable pseudo-emetric space.

name: Borel sigma-algebra of D[0,1] is that of the projections
statement:
SkorokhodSpace.measurableSpace_eq_comap_coeFn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [PseudoEMetricSpace E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] :
  SkorokhodSpace.instMeasurableSpace = MeasurableSpace.comap (fun x => ⇑x) MeasurableSpace.pi
scope_note: All projections, not a dense subset of times; second-countable values.

name: The Skorokhod space D[0,1] is Polish
statement:
SkorokhodSpace.instPolishSpace.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [EMetricSpace E] [CompleteSpace E]
  [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace E] : PolishSpace (SkorokhodSpace E)
scope_note: Complete separable (extended) metric E. The instance needs a metric on E, not only a Polish topology.

name: Tightness and fidi convergence give weak convergence in D[0,1]
statement:
SkorokhodSpace.tendsto_of_tendsto_map_restrict_of_isTight.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [MetricSpace E]
  [SecondCountableTopology E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  {μs : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (SkorokhodSpace E)}
  {μ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (SkorokhodSpace E)} {T : Set ↑unitInterval}
  (hT : Tᶜ.Countable) (h1 : 1 ∈ T)
  (hfdd :
    ∀ (J : Finset ↑unitInterval),
      ↑J ⊆ T →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (μs n).map fun x t => x ↑t) Filter.atTop
          (nhds (μ.map fun x t => x ↑t)))
  (htight : MeasureTheory.IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range fun n => ↑(μs n))) :
  Filter.Tendsto μs Filter.atTop (nhds μ)
scope_note: Fidi convergence on any T with countable complement containing 1. Time [0,1] only; the sufficient moment criteria for tightness are separate.
